package_info.package_manager: N/A (Injected JavaScript in e-commerce site HTML)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (Script block in live site HTML)
package_info.why_malicious: The script is a digital skimmer that exfiltrates sensitive customer data (address and credit card information) from the checkout page to a remote attacker-controlled server. This constitutes theft of payment data and a severe breach of user privacy and trust.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user loads and interacts with checkout page)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses credit card and address fields from the checkout form, serializes the data, and sends it via HTTP POST to a remote attacker-controlled server, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive payment and personal information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects sensitive user input (credit card and address) and transmits it to an external domain not associated with the legitimate e-commerce site.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal checkout page scripts should only process payment data for legitimate transaction purposes and never send it to unknown third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processors may collect form data, but only to trusted, vetted endpoints and with user consent.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive form fields (credit card, address)
Network request to untrusted external domain

attack_chain.action: Malicious script is injected into the checkout page HTML.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the skimmer code in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: Script executes in the user's browser, harvesting sensitive form data as the user enters it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of stolen data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is sent via HTTP POST to the attacker's remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and address information.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment or address form fields on checkout pages
Outbound network requests (POST) to domains not associated with the e-commerce site
Presence of obfuscated or minified inline scripts in sensitive page templates
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> blocks in checkout or payment page HTML
References to external JavaScript files from untrusted domains
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests from checkout pages to unknown or suspicious domains
Unusual traffic patterns from user browsers during checkout
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor checkout and payment page source for unauthorized or obfuscated script blocks. Use web application firewalls or browser instrumentation to detect JavaScript accessing sensitive form fields and making outbound requests to untrusted domains. Correlate network logs for POST requests containing payment data to domains not on an allowlist.
